title: Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Move Rotate **Objective** Move or rotate slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move **** ** Operation** **Move** 1. [Create a zipper.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115004529388-%EC%A7%80%ED%8D%BC-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its **Gizmo** appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the **Gizmo** to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. **Rotate** 1. With the**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the **Gizmo** changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. **※ Note:** To reset slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select [**Reset Slider Arrangement**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-ua/articles/115004681608) option. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for moving and rotating a zipper slider in a 3D garment design environment.

title: Register Custom OBJ as Button
content: Create Button OBJ Register Button OBJ Create Button OBJ by Thread Type ### **Objective** Register a custom OBJ file as Button. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0?si=H1MYv1aS1NI0W4RL&start=3417 **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Register Button ** Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024299748) ** Operation** **Create Button OBJ** Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. ** ※Required: ** ** ℹ️ From CLO 7.3, no 1, 2 requirements are not necessary and can be set at registration. ** * Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. e.g.) ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033429954) ![Button_OBJ.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033430114) Please check the attached OBJ file in your 3D modeling program for better understanding. ** ※Recommended: ** * Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. * The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in CLO. [ Button Property Setting ▶ Thread Length (cm)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005617768-%EB%8B%A8%EC%B6%94-%EC%86%8D%EC%84%B1-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95)) **Register Button OBJ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Register Button window appears. 2. After setting the following options, Click OK. **Property** | **Description****** ---|--- **Basic** | Set the name of the button file. **File** | **Size** | If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. **Size Name** | Set the size name. ** OBJ ** ** ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Select Mesh (ver 7.3) ** | Set the mesh for the buttons and thread. ** OBJ ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Width/Thickness** **/Weight** | Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. **Set as Default** | Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. **Axis Conversion (ver 7.3) ** | Switch axis of OBJ files in real time. **Preview (ver 7.3) ** | The imported OBJ file will be previewed. → The registered button is saved in the path below. CLO ▶ Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button **Create Button OBJ by Thread Type** 1. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to ***_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj.** 2. Register the created OBJ file as a button. 3. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. **C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button** 4. Run CLO and change the type of the thread in the button property window > Type > Thread Type.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to register a custom OBJ file as a button in CLO, ensuring proper setup and adherence to the required specifications for optimal performance.

title: Transform Graphic (3D)
content: **Transform Graphic (3D)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mRMopIL0VtA \- Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Material ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic (3D)** * **Scale Graphics ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFCd4pcwf-o \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The **Graphic Gizmo** will appear. \- Click and drag the arrow of the **Graphic Gizmo** to scale the selected Graphic. \- When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. - Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Graphic Transformation ▶ **Width** or **Height** to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to [Edit Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380188-Edit-Texture-3D-#Click4).) * **Rotate Graphics ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFCd4pcwf-o \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. \- Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. \- When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. * **Move Graphics** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Y6gCsykuaw \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the Graphic to move. \- When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive guidance on using the **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool to scale, rotate, and move graphics within a 3D environment, featuring instructional videos and step-by-step instructions.

title: Select

be selected and highlighted in yellow. \- The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. **Pattern Properties** YouTube Video: title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
content: **Objective** Use the **Trace** function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. ** Location** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644128/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644128/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** 2. Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being highlighted in yellow color. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines or Internal Lines. → A Pop-up menu appears. 4. Select **Trace as Internal** **Shape** or **Convert to Internal Shape** in the pop-up menu. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being traced as /converted to Internal Shapes.

title: Optimize All Curve Points
content: ### **Objective** Optimize the number of curve points on the segments to ease the Pattern editing proces. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CwB8_ad328M?si=9IO9xNl9i0JPloAU&start=1701 ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001059728/2.png)Edit Pattern** ### ** ****Operation** 1. Click the tool indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the 2D Pattern Window and click the **Optimize All Curve Points** , or right-click on the lines to optimize the curve points and click the **Optimize All Curve Points**. → Optimize Curve Points window appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver 7.2) 3. Adjust the ratio of curve points. → Closer to 0%, there will be fewer curve points, but there may be deviations from the original curvature.
content_description: This web page aims to provide a streamlined guide for optimizing curve points in 2D pattern editing, enhancing efficiency and precision in design modifications.

title: [Popup] Show/Hide Sewing
content: ### **Objective** When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. ** Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** /**Hide Sewing (All)** Object Browser ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** / **Hide Sewing (All)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** /**Hide Sewing (All)** Object Browser ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** / **Hide Sewing (All)** → The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window. **※ Note 1:** All Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) **Edit Sewing** tool is selected since the ![2D_________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115001219507/2D_________.png) **Show 2D Sewing** tool is activated automatically. **※ Note 2:** 2D Window ▶ Show Sewing icon ▶ **Show Sewing** (ver5.0 or later)

title: Flip Normal
content: **Objective** Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. ### ### **Location** Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ **Flip Normal** ### **Operation** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005480387/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool. 2. Select a Pattern to flip. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ **Flip Normal** → The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. **※ Note:** **Fold Angle** value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).
content_description: This web page provides a quick guide on how to efficiently flip the fabric surface of a pattern in Clo3D to streamline the sewing process.

title: Ruler and Guidelines (ver5.0.0 and Above)
content: **List of Contents** Ruler and Guidelines Edit Ruler Properties Edit Ruler's Starting Point Create Guidelines Create Guidelines (Use Point/Segment) Move Guidelines Delete Guidelines Lock Guidelines Show/Hide Guidelines **Ruler and Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vb_LLL41Nv0 \- Place 2D elements accurately to the needed position. \- Hover the mouse over the **2D Information Display** icon on the left top corner of the 2D window. Then, select the **Show Ruler** icon. \- Use the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360020752554/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Select/Move** tool or the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360020752574/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** tool to create the ruler. **Edit Ruler Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8RklRbC1Oac \- Set the ruler's unit. \- Right click on the ruler and select the desired unit from the right-click pop-up menu. \- The unit changes after the selection. **Edit Ruler's Starting Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UuSh9BnTKus \- Change the starting point of the ruler. \- Click and drag the intersection of the rulers at the left top corner. \- X and Y axes appear over the mouse cursor. The ruler resets to 0 starting from the point where the mouse cursor is released. \- Double click the intersection at the left top corner, to reset the starting point to the default. **Create Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oSW4uTYqon0 \- Click and drag either the X or Y-axis. \- Release the mouse to place the guideline to the desired position. \- Hit the Ctrl key while clicking and dragging the - axis to convert to a Y-axis guideline. The same works for the vice-versa. \- Click a X-axis guideline while holding down the Ctrl key to convert it to a Y-axis guideline. The same works for the vice-versa. **Create Guidelines (Use Point/Segment)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rR0mV71rrlc \- Right click on points (two points) or a segment to be a reference of a guideline. When the right-click pop-up menu appears, select **Create a Guideline Along Points**. **※ Note:** When using the **Create a Guideline Along Points** option, two can be selected for points whereas only one can be selected for segments. **Move Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=azZXPelAXWU \- Click and drag a guideline. \- When multiple guidelines are selected, only the one selected at last can be moved. **Delete Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBgR3WdDwZs \- Right click on the guideline to be deleted and select **Delete Guideline** or **Delete All Guidelines**. \- Click and drag the guideline to be deleted back to the ruler. **Lock Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PGgdLe37hEE \- Lock guidelines in place. \- Right click on the 2D window and select **Lock All Guidelines** from the pop-up menu. With the option, the guidelines are locked and cannot be selected and moved. **Show/Hide Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jO7IUo95cEw \- Show or hide guidelines as needed. \- Hover the mouse over the **2D Information Display** icon on the left top corner of the 2D window. Then, select the **Show Guideline** icon. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for utilizing rulers and guidelines in a 2D design environment, detailing their creation, modification, and management to ensure precise placement of elements.

title: Zipper Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Zipper Slider Gizmo Move Zipper Slider Rotate Zipper Slide **Zipper Slider Gizmo** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IlSYQXp7k7g \- Rotate or move slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape using its Gizmo. \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002238927/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png)**Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and select the slider. **Move Zipper Slider** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n1Qa9hlPaQc \- While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be moved to access the Gizmo. \- Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. \- Sliders cannot be moved vertically and horizontally. **Rotate Zipper Slide** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgWKCEM6J94 \- While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be rotated to access the Gizmo. \- Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on X axis. \- Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Y axis. \- Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Z axis. \- To rotate the puller only, click the puller again while the slider is selected. \- The puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes. \- To reset the slider’s position and angle, right click on the slider and select **Reset Slider Arrangement**. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions and video tutorials for manipulating zipper sliders using the Gizmo tool in 3D design software.

title: Seamline Topstitch
content: **Seamline TopstitchYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OWE8gjOvd4o ** **-** Establish the Topstitch along the Seamlines. \- Select the ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material ▶ **Seamline Topstitch**. \- With the Seamline Topstitch tool activated, all the Seamlines appear in the 2D Window. \- Hover over the desired Seamline. \- A blue guide point should appear and click and drag along the Seamline. \- Click again to complete the Seamline Topstitch. \- The Seamline Topstitch created on the Seamlines should be highlighted in red. \- The ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool creates the Topstitch along both sides of the paired Seamlines. Therefore, the blue guide point will appear on both sides of the paired Seamlines. \- The ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool has some similar qualities with the Free Topstitch tool. Users do not have to select the entire segment of the Seamline. Divide up the Seamlines to apply multiple styles of the Seamline Topstitch on the selected pair of the Seamlines.
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the Seamline Topstitch tool in our tutorial video to enhance your garment designs by creating detailed topstitches along seamlines.

title: Convert to Segment Point
content: **Convert to Segment Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=faDkVtmpBok \- Convert a curve point to a segment point \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911588/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a curve point and select **Convert to Segment Point** from the pop-up menu. ** **\- The selected curve point will be converted to a segment point.
content_description: Learn how to easily convert a curve point to a segment point in CLO 3D using the Edit Curve Point tool for precise design adjustments.

title: Show 2D Puckerings
content: **Show 2D Puckering** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MWoy0c1wpGY \- Show Puckerings in the 2D window even when Puckering tools are not in use. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022664487/mceclip0.png) **Show 2D Puckerings** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Materials ▶ **Show 2D Puckerings ** \- When the **Show 2D Puckerings** is activated, all Puckering lines will show and disappear from the 2D window.
content_description: This web page provides a guide on how to enable and display 2D Puckerings in the design window, enhancing visibility and control over puckering details in your projects.

title: Change Length
content: **Change Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tLdmNotDPw8 \- Change the length of a segment towards the start, end, or both directions. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022574087/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment to be edited and select **Change Length.** The Change Length window will appear. \- Select and modify below settings as needed. * * **Start YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tFFuU3x57eE \- **Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length Window. \- For Location, select **Start.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- The start point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. * **End ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8cHJ3sJJVb8 \- Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. \- For Location, select **End.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- The end point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. * **Both** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bzefu0NZk2s \- Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. \- For Location, select **Both.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- Both start and end points of the selected segment will be equally adjusted based on the designated length value.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to adjust the length of a segment in your design using the Change Length tool in the 2D window, complete with instructional videos for modifying the start, end, or both ends of the segment.

title: License Key Update
content: **List of Contents** License Key Update 1\. Creating a C2V file 2\. Updating a License Key using V2C file 3\. Double checking on updated License Key **License Key Update** **Objective** Set the dongle key when the Network License users want to update their dongle key info. (Currently only available on Windows PC) ** Operation** C2V file is a file sent from the users to CLO Support Team and V2C is the other way around. This method enables the users to update their account info / product type / the number of license without changing HASP dongle key. **Preparations ** →HASP dongle key →Upadate_License.exe file →C2V file →V2C file **1\. title: The patterns are deformed when I import my DXF file into CLO. How can I fix the problem?
content: **Question** When I import my DXF file into CLO selecting the 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing Line' setting, some of the patterns are deformed. How can I fix the problem? Example of deformation of a pattern: ![DXF1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058514333/DXF1.jpg) **Answer** The problem may occur when creating a pattern from 2D CAD software. Please firstly check two things below: 1. **If a sewing line or a cutting line of a pattern is made as 'Baseline' from 2D CAD program: ** If a pattern is created with 'Baselines' from 2D CAD program, the pattern might not be compatible with CLO. For patterns to be imported into CLO, it is recommended to create it with 'Outlines' instead of 'Baselines'. 2. **If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program:** If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program, it might not be compatible with CLO. The feature named 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line' is for importing a pattern into CLO by swapping sewing lines and cutting lines. However, as for patterns created as an unclosed shape, some of the patterns may be deformed when imported into CLO with 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line'. Thus, please firstly make sure whether a pattern is created as an unclosed shape or not. And if the former, modify the pattern to a closed shape and try to import it into CLO again. ![DXF2.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058514313/DXF2.jpg)
content_description: This webpage provides solutions for fixing pattern deformation issues when importing DXF files into CLO, specifically addressing the importance of using 'Outlines' instead of 'Baselines' and ensuring patterns are closed shapes.

title: Graphic Grading
content: **Graphic Grading** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5pjJ_OcNnjQ \- Apply grading rules to graphics added to Patterns. \- Load graphics to Patterns. \- Create a Grading Size. \- Select the ![grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001829027/grading.png)**Grading** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the graphic which grading rule is to be added and navigate to the Property Editor. \- Use the arrow keys on the keyboard or desired options to edit Distance or Offset. \- Grading rules applied to the graphic only changes its placement, but not size.

title: Shape Dart Cap
content: **Shape Dart Cap** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CdAULa8jnTY \- Smooth Pattern outlines with darts. \- Select the ![edit_pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001809048/edit_pattern.png)**Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** ** \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select two segments forming darts. \- Right-click on the select segments and select **Shape Dart Cap** from the pop-up menu. \- A black line appears showing how Pattern would look when darts are sewn. -Click and drag the red point on the black line to modify the curve as needed and hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- Pattern outlines with the dart are edited based on the modification. \- Dart’s folded Pattern outlines appear as Baselines.
content_description: Discover how to expertly use the Shape Dart Cap tool in our YouTube tutorial to refine pattern outlines with darts for precise garment design.
